metadata.note: Modern-day MBTA Commuter Rail network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://cdn.mbta.com/MBTA_GTFS.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added by researching each line's originating railroad and its milestone dates (line openings, corporate mergers, the 1964 creation of the MBTA and 1965 start of commuter subsidies, and modern restorations). Several lines carry REAL multi-decade gaps with no segments at all, because passenger service genuinely did not exist then: Fairmount 1944-1979, Kingston 1959-1997, Greenbush 1959-2007, Fall River/New Bedford ~1960-2025, and CapeFLYER 1959-2013. Unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, the older headway_min values are estimates, not real timetables.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
